settings.heading: About the cane collection
settings.text:
Cane furniture earned its reputation the hard way. Woven rattan has been used in furniture making for well over two centuries because it does something no solid panel can: it carries weight while staying light, and it breathes, so a chair back stays cool to lean against on a warm afternoon.

Every cane panel in this collection is woven by hand and set into a routed groove in the frame — the traditional method. It is slower and more expensive than gluing a sheet of machine-woven webbing onto the surface, and it is the difference between a panel that lasts decades and one that lifts at the edges within a year.

Choosing the right piece

  • For a small living room — the Heritage 2-Seater or the Dark Cane Bench Sofa. Both sit low with open frames, so they take up far less visual space than their footprint suggests.
  • For a reading corner — the Cane & Rattan Accent Chair. Compact enough for a landing or bedroom nook, with a deep linen seat.
  • For a bedroom refresh — the Cane Headboard pairs with an existing base, which is the cheapest way to change the character of a room.
  • For storage that isn't bulky — the cane-front sideboards. The woven doors keep the piece from reading as a solid block against the wall.

Caring for cane

Cane wants humidity. In a very dry room it can become brittle over years, so keep pieces away from a radiator or a direct heating vent. Dust with a dry brush and, if a panel starts to slacken slightly in summer, it will usually tighten again on its own as the air cools.
